title: What Country Am I In? Country From a Point
description: Identify the country for any point — What Country Am I In? reads boundary data by GPS or map click, disputed areas handled honestly. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a border-town click can land in either of two countries depending on which side of the river the pin drops — the page reports the boundary data's verdict for the exact point, not the town's reputation.
quick_answer: What Country Am I In? uses OpenStreetMap boundary data to identify the country a point falls in. Use your location or click the map and read the country field — the top of the administrative stack, answered from boundaries rather than from the nearest famous city.
steps_intro: The biggest boundary question, answered at the point:

body.t: Near frontiers, which side you are on decides roaming, currency and rules. The point's answer beats the road sign you passed a mile ago.
A dataset's country column gets audited point by point — disputed and coastal points surface exactly where audits should look.
, county, city — this page is the top slice of the same honest method.
Enclaves, exclaves and the world's odd corners become findable: click Baarle, Llívia or Kaliningrad and watch students' eyebrows.
Where boundaries are disputed, map data reflects one documented position. The page reports the data's country for the point; the FAQs name the caveat rather than hiding it.
Click the open ocean and there is no country to report — territorial waters complicate the shallows, but the honest open-sea answer is none.

faq: The page reports the country OpenStreetMap's boundary data assigns to the point, which follows the project's documented approach to disputed boundaries. It is a map answer, offered as such — the dispute itself belongs to diplomacy.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — click any point on earth instead of using GPS.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Country names and boundary renderings are political: short names, formal names and claims differ across sources and governments.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
The country identification follows boundary data; ISO country codes are the standard companions and the related tools surface them where the data carries them.
Boundary data centres on land territory. A point just offshore can read as no-country while lying in territorial waters — the dataset's scope, stated plainly.
No sovereign country governs it (treaty system instead); the page reports the absence honestly.
